'''Arts and culture'''
*[[LGBTQ rights in the United Kingdom]]
**King [[Charles III]] dedicates a memorial to [[LGBTQ]] members of the [[British Armed Forces|Armed Forces]] at the [[National Memorial Arboretum]] in [[Lichfield]], [[Staffordshire]], [[United Kingdom]], on the 25-year anniversary of the end to [[Sexual orientation and the military of the United Kingdom|the country's ban on gay servicemen]]. [https://apnews.com/article/king-charles-uk-lgbt-troops-memorial-29d3c25097dc08e3f43e250f2313bd08 (AP)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Taxation in Malta]]
**[[Malta]] introduces [[tax cut]]s exempting parents of two or more children from income tax on up to [[Euro|€]]18,500 ([[United States dollar|US$]]21,574) of earnings from 2026, rising to €30,000 ($34,985) by 2028, as part of efforts to address [[Demographics of Malta|its low fertility rate]]. [https://www.reuters.com/markets/us/malta-cuts-taxes-parents-bid-revive-native-birth-rate-2025-10-27/ (Reuters)]

*[[Montenegro–Turkey relations]]
**[[Montenegro]] suspends its [[Visa policy of Montenegro|visa-free arrangement]] for [[Turkish citizen]]s after the stabbing of a local man allegedly by Turkish nationals led to unrest in [[Podgorica]]. '''Law and crime'''
*A court in [[Mali]] sentences former [[List of prime ministers of Mali|prime minister]] [[Moussa Mara]] to two years in prison on charges of undermining state security and inciting public disorder. Mara will serve one year without [[parole]] and one year as a [[suspended sentence]]. [https://apnews.com/article/mali-prime-minister-moussa-mara-politics-prison-566a1fc387ee6f4ba480e7068777ea9f (AP)]
